API reference

Web

Flask analysis page with Pull Data and Update Analysis buttons.

Built by the create_app factory so tests can construct an isolated application that reads fake rows and starts a fake scraper. Run from src/: flask –app app run

app.heading(column)[source]
app.build_blocks(results)[source]

Shape each question’s rows so one template block renders all of them.

app.database_analysis()[source]

Read the eleven answers and the row count from PostgreSQL as (blocks, total).

app.spawn_pull()[source]

Start pull_data.py in its own process and return the handle.

class app.PullState(runner=None)[source]

Busy state for the Pull Data button, kept on an instance so tests can inject a fake.

running()[source]

Return True while a started pull is still alive.

start()[source]

Start a pull and remember the process.

died_quietly()[source]

Return True when the last pull exited non-zero without a status file.

app.last_pull(status_path, state)[source]

Summarize the most recent pull, or None when nothing is known.

app.wants_json()[source]

Answer button posts with JSON unless the caller ranks HTML higher, as browsers do.

app.create_app(config=None, *, analysis_source=None, pull_runner=None)[source]

Build the app, letting tests override config and inject fake data and scraper callables.

ETL

Scrape Grad Cafe results with headless Firefox and parse them with BeautifulSoup.

scrape.extract_records(soup) → list[dict][source]

Extracts admission records from the html.

scrape.get_next(soup, url) → str[source]

Returns the URL for the next page from the html.

scrape.scrape_data()[source]

Pull applicant data from Grad Cafe.

Reshape scraped Grad Cafe records into the cleaned applicant format.

clean.clean_data(records) → list[dict][source]

Converts scraped records into the cleaned, structured format.

clean.save_data(records, path=PosixPath('/Users/girlenginerd/Desktop/jhu-software-eng-python/module_4/src/applicant_data.json'))[source]

Saves the cleaned records as a single JSON file.

clean.load_data(path=PosixPath('/Users/girlenginerd/Desktop/jhu-software-eng-python/module_4/src/applicant_data.json')) → list[dict][source]

Loads the cleaned records back from the JSON file.

Pull Data: scrape the newest Grad Cafe pages and load them into PostgreSQL.

pull_data.save_raw(records, path)[source]

Append records whose URL is not already in the Module 2 scrape file.

Database and queries

SQLAlchemy model and session factory for the applicants table.

class models.Base(**kwargs: Any)[source]

Base class for SQLAlchemy models.

class models.Applicant(**kwargs)[source]

One Grad Cafe submission in the existing applicants table.

models.database_url()[source]

Return the connection URL, preferring DATABASE_URL over the PG* variables.

models.make_engine(url=None)[source]

Build an engine for the URL, timing out only on PostgreSQL connections.

models.configure(url)[source]

Point the shared Session at another database, so tests can override it.

Load cleaned Module 2 applicant JSON into PostgreSQL using PG* environment variables.

load_data.as_text(value, key)[source]

Trim text, treating only null and blank as missing.

load_data.as_number(value, key)[source]

Parse a score, accepting Module 2’s labelled form such as “GPA 3.40”.

load_data.as_date(value, key)[source]

Parses the date formats from the grad cafe json.

load_data.to_row(record, position)[source]

Convert one Module 2 record into a row of column values.

load_data.read_records(path)[source]

Read and validate the whole file before any database changes.

load_data.dedup_key(row)[source]

Identify a submission by its URL, or by the whole row when it has none.

load_data.load_records(conn, rows)[source]

Append unseen rows atomically and return (inserted, skipped).

Answer the eleven analysis questions in raw SQL and print them.

Run from src/: python query_data.py. Connection settings come from DATABASE_URL or the PG* environment variables.

query_data.format_value(value, column)[source]

Display missing values, whole-number counts and two-decimal scores.

query_data.print_result(number, cursor)[source]

Print one line per question; separate multiple result rows with semicolons.

The eleven analysis questions as SQLAlchemy queries, shared with the Flask page.

orm_queries.matches_university(column)[source]

Recognize the four universities, including MIT as a whole word.

orm_queries.run_queries(session)[source]

Return each question’s result rows for console output or Flask.

orm_queries.format_value(value, column)[source]

Use the same formatting as query_data.py.
